a methodology has been developed in order to analyse the costs of a FOWF and the most important cost in each phase of the LCS is identified.
the most important costs for floating wind farms are: installation, exploitation, design and definition.
the life cycle cost analysis of FOWFs can be used in the decision-making process to determine the most appropriate platform and location.

the development of a methodology to evaluate the life cycle cost of a FOWF.
the development of a methodology that allows us to analyse the costs of a FOWF and the different phases that it goes through during its life cycle.

the following objectives: to analyse the cost breakdown structure of a floating offshore wind farm and to determine the key variables that affect the total cost of the life cycle; to analyse the influence of the floating platform on the cost breakdown structure; to determine the most important phases of the floating offshore wind farm life cycle; to determine the influence of the location of the floating offshore platform on the cost of the floating wind farm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important costs for a Floating Offshore wind farm are the costs of the floating platform, the foundation, the installation and the operation and maintenance.

the most expensive phase of the life-cycle is the manufacturing phase, and the most expensive cost is the installation cost, which is due to the high costs of installation in the sea, the high costs of the installation of the floating platform and the high costs of transportation of the wind turbines to the installation point.
floating wind farms are economically competitive with the current costs of electricity generation.

it is a tool that will allow us to make decisions about the future development of floating wind farms.

we have developed a methodology to analyse the life cycle costs of floating offshore wind platforms and we have applied it to three different types of floating platforms: semisubmerged, spar and Tensioned Leg Platforms (TLP).
the most important costs for the life cycle of a floating wind farm are the costs related to the manufacturing of the wind turbine and the floating platform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most important cost in a FOWF is not the floating structure, but the installation and the operation and maintenance of the wind turbines.
the most expensive phase of the life-cycle of a floating offshore wind farm is the design and manufacturing phase.
the most important cost is the installation cost, and the second is the manufacturing cost.
